g.text: Left: the experiment that produced Chinchilla — sweep model size at fixed compute and read off the minimum. Right: note that the

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: published fit's own optimum (blue) runs from about 30 to 95 tokens per parameter and never meets the paper's 20:1 headline (green).

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: That inconsistency in the published Approach-3 constants is real and documented; the 20:1 rule comes from the paper's other two

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: methods. Either way, deployed models (orange) sit far above both, because the cost that matters to them is inference, not training.
